criteria.note: docs/method.md carries a clean-context dispatch rule for the multi-spec / autonomous loop: the long-lived orchestrator MUST be a thin dispatcher, each spec's build and review run in a fresh dispatched sub-context that returns only a compact receipt, the orchestrator keeps only that receipt and never ingests a sub-context's transcript. The rule names its rationale (the 2026-07-19 OOM where one inline orchestrator reached roughly 17.8 GB and was killed by the kernel). Docs hygiene sweeps pass over the new prose and the section is generic.

plugin/skills/run/SKILL.md step 5 is now an explicit fresh-context sub-agent dispatch of the warp-reviewer with parity to the build in step 2 (both name their dispatched sub-agent, neither shares the other's context), and a CLEAN-CONTEXT DISPATCH paragraph states the orchestrator retains only each step's receipt (verdict plus findings, not the reviewer's transcript) and points to the method loop rule (section 2.7.1) for chaining many specs. Docs sweeps pass.

A pure receipt projection ships at the dispatch boundary: .warp/work.py RECEIPT_FIELDS plus dispatch_receipt(outcome) returns a new dict of only the allowlisted summary fields present in the outcome (spec, kind, ok, status, verdict, commit, proof_digest, gate, halted_at, reason) and drops everything else (a full nested result, a transcript, a fat land record). It fails closed (allowlist not denylist) and is the value the loop retains per spec.

The selftest enforces the receipt contract with real teeth. Over a realistic bulky outcome (a nested executor result plus a 20 KB transcript) it asserts the projected receipt keys stay within the allowlist and the serialized size is under a fixed small bound (_RCPT_MAX_BYTES 2048); the two TEETH checks take the SAME bulky outcome through a passthrough projection and are REJECTED (allowlist breached and size bound blown), so the assertions are not vacuous. I confirmed the teeth are real by live mutation: mutating dispatch_receipt to a passthrough drove the selftest RED, then reverted clean.

.warp/executor.py LoopSteps.build and LoopSteps.review docstrings and .warp/dispatch.py's module docstring state the clean-context / receipt contract explicitly (the delegated step runs in a fresh sub-context and the orchestrator retains only a compact receipt via work.py dispatch_receipt / RECEIPT_FIELDS, never the transcript, naming the 2026-07-19 OOM this cures). The dispatch selftest block still passes unchanged, so the docstring edits alter no behavior.

findings.text: Non-blocking. dispatch_receipt is a codified, reusable projection utility for the agent-driven loop (the thin orchestrator applies it per spec); it is deliberately NOT wired into the mechanical WorkLoop.step, consistent with the spec's out-of-scope (no change to the mechanical dispatch's routing, status flips, or gate/proof/land behavior). The receipt boundary is therefore enforced by the contract and its teeth-test rather than by a call site inside WorkLoop; wiring it into a live loop is the adopter/loop-orchestrator step. Recorded as a note, not a defect.

summary: WARP-0909 (the clean-context dispatch loop, a standalone spec) passes with notes at a2423c7, zero blocking findings. The method (section 2.7.1) and the run skill (step 5) now make the multi-spec loop a thin dispatcher that keeps only a compact receipt per spec and never ingests a sub-context's transcript, naming the 2026-07-19 OOM it cures (AC1, AC2).
